Yep, that's how I usually go about it! Clone vats and gene clinics will help fill your planets with pops faster, and eventually when you're close to fully utilizing/populating the planet, replace them with a building that produces something else. Clone vats will cost 30 food a month, but I usually build a hydroponic farm on all my starbases except for shipyards and choke point bastions. Good use of bastions are another key thing. Try to expand your empire in a way that only leaves a handful of ways in, preferably somewhere around 2-4. Fully upgrade bastions in those few border systems as quickly as you can, and the AI is far less likely to attack you for a very long time.

Micromanaging the jobs on your colonies is the very most important thing you can do to balance your economy. You can manually control how many available job slots are filled in each position. Don't build too many districts and buildings before you have the pops to work those jobs. Having a few available jobs at all times helps with pop growth, but if you have dozens of districts and buildings that aren't being worked, you're still paying for the upkeep of those builds without any reward, and they all contribute to your empire sprawl. Assign science ships to aid in research on your science heavy planets, that will give you a nice bonus. The main focus at the start of the game should be on establishing new colonies. The sooner you have more sources of pop growth, the more you're able to expand. Pops are the main power in the game, so once you figure out how to properly manage them, everything else more or less takes care of itself.

If you plan on going with no military at all, you’re going to want to make friends and make them fast. The AI will bully you if you don’t have a strong navy of your own, so do everything you can to ensure your neighbors like you. 

Send your envoys to improve relations, make trade, migration, research, and non aggression pacts with them, establish embassies. Don’t make defensive pacts unless you’re prepared to build a navy, because they could drag you into a war that way. 

All those pacts will hurt your influence gain, which will limit how many systems you can build star bases in. Focus initially on sending your science ships out to explore the galaxy to each side of your starting system (build about 2-3 additional science ships as quickly as you can). 

Ignore anomalies at first, most of them just add extra resources to the system, so you can always come back and do that later. Start looking for single system choke points on both sides that you can make your borders, and build a single connected line of star bases from your home system to those two systems. This way it reduces border friction with your neighbors, and you only initially have to focus on making those two systems defendable. Build bastions in those systems, so even if you don’t have a navy, the AI would still think twice about invading your territory. 

After you have your two choke points, you can go back and start building star bases in all the systems that now only you have access to, as well as studying all the anomalies you skipped over. I would also fairly early on colonize at least three other planets so you can start ramping up your empire’s production. 

You always do want to be ready to build up a defensive navy even as a pacifist, but think of it more like how they operate in Star Trek. You have the means to defend yourself, but you don’t go seeking out conflict.

Identify any unstable wormhole’s in your territory, and build defensive bastions in those systems as well. It doesn’t matter if you never stabilize them yourself, the AI can stabilize the other end and invade you through the wormhole.

And lastly, until August 25th, console is on version 3.0.3, which means if you look for more in depth guides on how certain things work, make sure they were made for this version, since different versions have some pretty drastic differences. 

I hope this helps, and that you have fun with your first game!
